Conflict: In-Service Agent recommends high-durability impact-resistant virgin ABS to prevent premature physical degradation and microplastic release, while Circularity Agent recommends single-polymer unpainted polypropylene to maximize recyclability.
Decision: Single-polymer high-strength ABS with recycled content
Rationale: This decision balances engineering feasibility and regulatory compliance. High-strength ABS provides the necessary impact resistance to prevent premature failure (durability), satisfying ESPR Annex I (a), while using a single-polymer with recycled content avoids the contamination of recycling streams caused by multi-material overmolding, satisfying ESPR Annex I (d) and (h).

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends automated ultrasonic welding or simple snap-fits to minimize production complexity and energy, while In-Service Agent rejects permanent joining methods because they prevent non-destructive disassembly for repair.
Decision: Threaded fasteners (screws) with metal inserts combined with reversible snap-fits
Rationale: Under the priority hierarchy, regulatory compliance is a non-negotiable requirement that overrides manufacturing cost and cycle time. ESPR Annex I (b) mandates ease of repair and maintenance through non-destructive disassembly, which requires reversible mechanical fasteners rather than permanent ultrasonic welding.

Conflict: Material and Design Agent recommends a rare-earth-free synchronous reluctance motor to avoid critical raw materials and substances of concern, while In-Service Agent recommends a brushless DC motor to maximize energy efficiency and technical lifetime.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; In-Service Agent
Decision: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor designed with a modular architecture for easy extraction of rare-earth magnets and copper windings
Rationale: Energy efficiency (g) and technical lifetime (a) are primary in-service performance parameters that must be optimized for vacuum cleaners. To comply with both energy efficiency mandates and critical raw material recovery goals, a BLDC motor is selected but must be designed for non-destructive disassembly to allow clean extraction of magnets and copper at end-of-life.

Conflict: In-Service Agent recommends an active cooling fan with a thermal cut-out switch to prevent motor overheating and extend lifetime, while Circularity Agent recommends passive cooling to avoid thermal interface materials and potting compounds that contaminate recycling streams.
Decision: Active cooling fan integrated on motor shaft with thermal cut-out switch, implemented without chemical potting compounds or adhesives
Rationale: Engineering feasibility and reliability dictate that active cooling is required to prevent motor burnout under continuous heavy loads, supporting durability (a) and functional performance (s). To address circularity concerns, the thermal cut-out switch and fan will be mounted using mechanical fasteners rather than chemical potting compounds or thermal pastes.

Conflict: Manufacture Agent recommends a monolithic integrated chassis to simplify assembly and reduce manufacturing waste, while Circularity Agent recommends a fully modular architecture with toolless swappable blocks to facilitate repair, upgrading, and remanufacturing.
Decision: Fully modular architecture with toolless swappable functional blocks
Rationale: ESPR Annex I (b) and (c) mandate design for repairability, remanufacturing, and upgrading. A monolithic design is rejected because it causes premature obsolescence of the entire product when a single component fails, which directly violates regulatory compliance. The long-term waste reduction of modularity outweighs short-term manufacturing simplicity.

Conflict: In-Service Agent highlights that battery power is required for optimal mobility and functional performance, while Circularity Agent rejects batteries due to end-of-life hazardous waste and safety hazards.
Decision: Mains-powered corded (AC) with a modular, retractable cord reel
Rationale: While cordless battery-powered options offer higher mobility, the regulatory focus on minimizing hazardous waste (r) and environmental footprint (m) under ESPR, combined with the extreme durability and reliability (a) of corded power (avoiding battery degradation), justifies a corded design. To mitigate mobility limitations, a long, high-flexibility cord with a modular, easily repairable retractable reel will be implemented.
